models.title: Signed error of a sample estimate
models.summary: The owner defines sampling error as the difference between a sample statistic and the population quantity estimated.

relationship.original_equation: Signed sampling error = sample estimate − population parameter
relationship.locator: Chapter 9, Classical Parameter Estimation, printed p69, Terminology Regarding Estimators
relationship.translation_notes: This profile uses dimensionless quantities; a monetary or physical parameter needs a corresponding shared-unit profile.

variables.context: Same estimand, population, sampling design and dimensionless unit profile
Same estimand, population, sampling design and dimensionless unit profile
Same estimand, population, sampling design and dimensionless unit profile

assumptions: The statistic and parameter estimate the same population quantity with the same units and reference period.
The parameter is supplied or known for the calculation; it is generally unknown in a real application.
limitations: The sign convention is explicitly estimate minus parameter; reversing the convention reverses the sign.
A realized estimation error is not the estimator’s sampling bias, standard error, or total survey error.

models.title: Bias of an estimator
models.summary: The owner describes unbiasedness by equality of the estimator’s sampling expectation and its target parameter; signed bias is their difference.

relationship.original_equation: Estimator bias = expected estimator value − population parameter
relationship.locator: Chapter 9, Classical Parameter Estimation, printed p69, Terminology Regarding Estimators
relationship.translation_notes: This profile uses dimensionless quantities; other estimands need corresponding shared-unit profiles.

variables.context: Same estimand, population, sampling design and dimensionless unit profile
Same estimand, population, sampling design and dimensionless unit profile
Same estimand, population, sampling design and dimensionless unit profile

assumptions: The expectation exists and is computed over the declared sampling distribution for the specified estimator and population parameter.
Expected estimate and parameter use the same unit profile and estimand.
limitations: Bias is a property of an estimator under a sampling model, not the realized error of one sample.
Zero bias alone does not imply low variance, consistency, efficiency or absence of other error.
